doc.title: Barry Harris — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: How the singing classes and choir began
summary: His choir came from the jazz culture theater, learning to sing phrases in class and to teach lyrics.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: So now, how does your choir life, with the choirs that you’ve had. How – what’s the history of that?
That’s just – that came from the jazz culture theater. See, I had – I started singing classes. See, I had horn classes, I had singing classes. I couldn’t sing, I couldn’t even

hum phrases for them to be able to get them, you know. When I noticed a change was when there was a – there was a trumpet player – he’s still around, too, Bobby Rogovin, he had a good ear. And so, maybe in my second year or something, in my third year or something. I started singing the phrases, and he started playing them right back at me. I said, “aha!” See, so I knew that I improved there, you know? And then dealing with the singers – learning lyrics, teaching singing, teaching phasing and stuff, you learn yourself, that’s all. So I just learned myself, that’s all.
So you – you know a lot of lyrics to a lot of songs?
Yeah, I know a lot of lyrics to songs. I know – it’s weird. A whole lot of lyrics – they come back.
